pages.text: The district quiz contest began at ten o’clock. Three tables sat on the stage, each with a buzzer and a bell. Godfred, Lamisi and Raymond sat at the table for Okuapem Basic. Raymond’s knees knocked together. “Breathe,” said Lamisi. “We prepared. We trust each other. Let us just do our best.”
sentences: The district quiz contest began at ten o’clock.

Godfred, Lamisi and Raymond sat at the table for Okuapem Basic.
Raymond’s knees knocked together.
“Breathe,” said Lamisi.
“We prepared.
We trust each other.
Let us just do our best.”
pages.alt: Three students sit at a quiz table on a stage with a buzzer and a bell.

pages.text: Madam Nortey, the quizmaster, read the first question. “What is the next prime number after 13?” Godfred’s hand shot to the buzzer. “Seventeen,” he said. “Correct,” said Madam Nortey. The audience clapped. In the next round, Lamisi answered a question about the water cycle and Raymond answered one about the Volta River. Okuapem Basic led by two points.

“What is the next prime number after 13?” Godfred’s hand shot to the buzzer.
“Seventeen,” he said.
“Correct,” said Madam Nortey.
The audience clapped.
In the next round, Lamisi answered a question about the water cycle and Raymond answered one about the Volta River.
Okuapem Basic led by two points.
pages.alt: A boy presses a buzzer as the quizmaster reads from a card and the audience applauds.

pages.text: But the quiz was close. Another school caught up, then pulled ahead. In the third round, Godfred buzzed too fast and gave the wrong answer. “Minus two,” said Madam Nortey. Godfred’s face fell. Raymond whispered, “It is fine. We all make mistakes. Wait for the next question.” Godfred nodded and took a deep breath.

pages.alt: A boy covers his face after a wrong answer while his teammate whispers to him.

pages.text: In the last round, the scores were tied. Madam Nortey held up the final card. “Which scientist is known for the theory of gravity?” Lamisi leaned in. “Newton,” she whispered. Raymond nodded. But Godfred wondered whether it was a trick question. The other school buzzed first and answered. “Isaac Newton,” they said. “Correct.” The hall roared.

pages.alt: Three students whisper at a table while another team’s hand presses a buzzer.

pages.text: Okuapem Basic lost by one point. Godfred felt his throat tighten. “I should have buzzed,” he said. “If I had trusted my first thought...” Lamisi put a hand on his shoulder. “We prepared,” she said. “We lost by one point, but we got many answers right. And you gave us the lead in the first round.” Raymond added, “We won as a team and we lost as a team.”

pages.text: They walked across the stage and shook hands with the winning team. “Well done,” said Godfred. “That last question was ours, but you were quicker.” The other captain smiled. “You were tough,” she said. “See you next year.” Madam Nortey came over with the certificates. “Participation is not a small thing,” she said. “You learned today, and learning is the real prize.”

pages.alt: Students shake hands across a stage while a quizmaster holds certificates.

pages.text: That evening, Raymond wrote to Madam Nortey. Because she was an older person he knew, he wrote a semi-formal letter, with his address and the date at the top. “House 11, Cedar Road, Aburi. 12th June, 2027. Dear Madam Nortey, I hope you are well. I am writing to thank you for organising the district quiz. Although our team came second, we learned a great deal, and we are already revising for next year. Thank you for your kindness and patience. Yours sincerely, Raymond Laryea.”

pages.alt: A boy writes a thank-you letter at a desk beside a certificate.

pages.text: Exam-safe tip: Raymond wrote a short, polite letter with a clear reason for writing, in full words. He wrote “thank you” and not “tnx” or “ty”. Notice also that he did not say “we lost lol”. He wrote “we learned a great deal”. A positive tone helps even when the news is not winning. The end.
